notes:
A notch on a curved edge reaches the cutting files; a damaged licence file does not stop the program [skip ci]

From the independent review of 2026-11 (each reproduced first):
- LEVEL7 and MTM puts a notch where the sewing line's point, moved out by the seam allowance, lies; its cut line is a
  polyline, so on a curve the notch starts a few hundredths of a millimetre beside it. The PLT and the ISO take a notch
  only when it starts on the cut line (0.01 mm): such a notch was left out of both files without a word, and counted
  as cut. The reader of the order's file now moves the notch onto the cut line (direction and length kept); moved by
  more than 0.5 mm it is said in the file's issues, further than 10 mm the file is refused. The owner's own design was
  inside the limit (0.003 mm at most): nothing of it was lost; the margin was thin.
- the cutting files count the notches they really cut; one left out is said («notches_left_out», a warning line).
- a licence file damaged or written by hand, or a folder that cannot be written for a moment, stopped the program and
  its command line with a traceback: each counts as empty, the program goes on.
A model of GRAFIS is read and cut exactly as before (its reference files unchanged).
(Build 19 stopped on the new test itself: it wrote its DXF as text, which Windows gives other line ends — the file is
written as bytes now; the command line's gate is asked with the key in the licence tests.)
